item.title: Assembly Drill 2026-11-20: crackme
item.description:
# Crackme: find the password (Windows x64, arg in rcx)
`rcx` holds a pointer to a null-terminated ASCII string.
``` check: movzx eax, word ptr [rcx] ; load 2 bytes at once xor eax, 0x2020 cmp eax, 0x6B6F jne fail cmp byte ptr [rcx+2], 0 jne fail mov eax, 1 ret fail: xor eax, eax ret ```
`word ptr [rcx]` reads the first two characters as one 16-bit number. x86 is little-endian: the byte at the lower address (the first character) becomes the *low* byte of the number. Which string makes `check` return 1?
---
**Answer:** `"OK"`
1. Undo the xor (it's self-inverse): 0x6B6F ^ 0x2020 = 0x4B4F, so the loaded word must be 0x4B4F. 2. Little-endian: low byte 0x4F ('O') is the first character, high byte 0x4B ('K') is the second — reading the hex left to right gives "KO", which is backwards. 3. The `[rcx+2] == 0` check forces exactly two characters. (Bonus: xor 0x20 flips ASCII case, so the constant 0x6B6F is just "ok" in lowercase.)
